factsAccepted: Blended ARR grows 22% with EBITDA only 8%; the growth is carried by the SMB segment (+28%) which is under-monetized, while the higher-ARPU large-group segment grows just 5%. NRR is 98% blended, below the >105% bar investors expect at Series B, indicating weak expansion rather than a logo-churn problem (churn 2%).

Logo retention is strong (2% quarterly churn) but expansion is weak, especially in SMB (segment NRR ~99%). The company keeps customers but does not grow them, which is a go-to-market/monetization signal, not a satisfaction or quality failure.

Single-customer concentration (300-office DSO = 12% of ARR, top 10 = 35%) with annual renewal and pricing leverage creates a real downside risk, but the DSO segment is only growing 5% — chasing more large-group concentration would worsen risk and offers limited growth.

Sales and product are optimized for large multi-location deals; SMB self-serve onboarding and packaging are underdeveloped, which plausibly explains low SMB ARPU and expansion despite strong SMB logo growth.

Win/loss and pricing-elasticity data for the SMB segment (would higher ARPU/packaging hold?).
